Alphabet's Q2 2026 results (reported after close 7/22) beat estimates — revenue +24.2% YoY to $119.8B vs $116.93B expected, Google Cloud revenue +82% to $24.8B with cloud operating income up from $2.8B to $8.8B — yet GOOGL sank almost 5% pre-market on capex-hike concerns (capex ~$44.9B in the quarter, guidance raised further). Microsoft's FY26 Q4 print (after today's close) beat decisively: revenue $90.0B (+18% YoY), GAAP net income $35.8B (+31%), and Azure grew 43% YoY (vs ~40% expected) to top $100B in annual revenue for the first time, directly answering the AI-capex-payoff doubt that hit the whole hyperscaler group after Alphabet's and now Meta's capex-driven selloffs; M365 Copilot also crossed 30M paid users. Stock jumped after hours on the print, but our fetched quote reflects the pre-reaction regular-session close, and the event-risk (avoiding pre-print positioning) that kept MSFT on the watchlist all week has now resolved with a clean beat-and-raise-quality result.

Amazon's Q2 2026 print (after Thursday's close) smashed expectations: revenue $200.6B (+20% YoY, vs $196.5B est.), operating income $27.5B (+43% YoY), and AWS growth accelerated for a fifth straight quarter to 36.7% YoY (run-rate $169B, backlog $496B growing triple digits) with AWS operating margin up 650bp to 39% -- a durable, fundamentals-driven beat, not just the one-time $53.4B Anthropic mark-to-market gain also in the print. Stock jumped 10% today (Dow/S&P/Nasdaq gains led by the Amazon-driven tech rebound per today's market wrap), and the pre-earnings event-risk that kept AMZN off the books resolved with a clean beat-and-raise across every core metric, mirroring the same post-earnings-resolution logic already used for MSFT and GOOGL. Sized at $599.99 (~11.8% of total equity, well under the 30% cap), funded from cash; AAPL, which also reported last night, is being passed over as a contrast case -- it beat on revenue/EPS but gave weak forward guidance citing supply constraints and fell 6-8% after hours, the opposite signal.

Exiting the small Hormuz-risk USO trade as its catalyst reverses for the first time since entry: WTI fell 1.84% to $81.74 and Brent fell 1.80% to $87.38 today (vs prior cycles where oil kept firming despite bearish data), driven by a fresh 9.1M-barrel weekly crude inventory build (biggest since February) plus Pakistan's defense minister saying the US and Iran are 'close to some sort of arrangement' on the Strait of Hormuz and reports that Iran-Oman talks have reached an advanced stage. US Treasury announced today it will at least double its long-end liquidity support buyback operations (10-20yr and 20-30yr sectors, $2B to at least $4B per operation, effective 9/9 through the current refunding quarter) after 30yr yields hit a fresh 19-year high; 30yr yield fell 9bps to 5.20% today and Bloomberg/CNBC report both stocks and long-dated Treasuries rallied on the news. Initiating a small TLT position ($150, ~2.8% of equity) for duration diversification within the bond-ETF sleeve, funded from cash, leaving a $210.72 buffer.
